title: enforce-service-residency-and-kms-origin-audit-gate
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a residency-proof enforcement middleware, RBACv2 binding generator for service-account->KMS mapping, and an audit gating step which rejects requests missing verified KMS-origin claims. Backwards-compatible by default; rollout gated behind feature flag redwood.residency_enforcer.
description: Summary: This PR implements a residency-aware enforcement path that ties service identity, declared residency, and permitted KMS backends into a single enforcement gate at ingress. Motivation: customers in regulated regions require proof that encryption operations and key usage are bound to allowed geographic providers and that access is auditable. The change set introduces: 1) a residency-proof middleware that validates a signed residency assertion attached to requests and annotates the authz context with residency claims; 2) a RBACv2 binding generator that compiles operator-provided residency policies into per-service allowed-KMS lists; 3) a KMS-origin-assertion header verifier and selector to ensure outgoing key operations use an approved provider; 4) an audit gate which stamps residency verification and KMS origin into the immutable audit envelope and rejects requests lacking required proofs when policy mandates; 5) migration helpers and a simulator to preview policy effects before enforcement. Checklist: [x] Add residency middleware and unit tests; [x] Add RBACv2 binding compiler and integration tests; [x] Add KMS selector and provider unit tests; [x] Add audit envelope augmentation and end-to-end tests; [x] Add docs and upgrade notes; [ ] Feature flag rollout gating in infra (follow-up infra task). Rollout plan: land behind feature flag redwood.residency_enforcer=false by default; run policy-sim in canary; enable enforcement for audited organizations only initially. Important implementation notes: residency assertions are JWT-like signed blobs generated by regional attestors (or customer-provided attestations). The middleware verifies signatures using configured attestor keys, canonicalizes the residency claim, and stores canonical residency tags on the request context used by RBACv2 decisions. The RBACv2 compiler accepts residency policies in YAML (examples/docs updated) and emits a compact allowlist keyed by service account and route. The KMS selector consults the allowlist and attempts to route requests to the highest-priority compatible provider; when none are available and policy requires residency, the request is rejected with 403 and an audit entry. The audit gate now writes an immutable residency.kms provenance field into the sealed audit envelope so downstream compliance tooling can consume it. Migration and safety: added a policy-simulator mode that runs decisions non-blocking and logs samples for 7 days; operators can use the simulator to refine policies before flipping enforcement. Related work items: ENG-21234 (policy compiler), ENG-21240 (audit envelope extension), SUP-4421 (customer support case for EU key pinning).

review_comments: Evelyn Chen: Overall design looks solid. Request: split the residency assertion verification into a reusable package so other components can call it outside the ingress path.
Maya Patel (author): Good catch — factored verification into pkg/attestor/verify.go and updated imports across ingress and tests.
Arjun Rao: Security review: ensure attestor key rotation is handled. Also validate token expiry and nonce replay protections.
Maya Patel (author): Added key-rotation hooks and nonce cache with TTL; spelled out in docs and added unit tests for replay attempt.
Lucia Morales: CI flake on e2e in the first run — seems related to provider_registry caching under test harness. Please ensure deterministic provider availability in tests.
Maya Patel (author): Fixed tests to inject a deterministic provider registry mock and added an integration test harness reset step. Reran CI and all green.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag redwood.residency_enforcer default=false. To preview policies use rbactl simulate --policy-file <yaml> which runs non-blocking simulator and writes samples to /var/log/redwood/policy-sim. Attestor public keys are configured via ConfigMap deploy/helm/redwood/templates/configmap-residency.yaml. When enabling enforcement, coordinate with KMS providers and ensure provider tags match residency codes. Rolling back: flip flag to false and restart ingress to revert to non-blocking path.
incident_tie_in: This PR addresses SUP-4421 (customer-reported illegal key usage across EU/US boundaries) by providing an enforcement mechanism and auditable provenance. No active incident in flight; implemented as proactive compliance work.
testing_notes: Added e2e tests that run in the perf-canary lab with a three-node mocked provider setup: eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1. Tests exercise positive and negative enforcement cases and policy simulator logging. Recommended nightly job: run rbactl simulate across sample tenant policies to detect unintended denies.
